sections.skill: Use federal and state consumer protections and file a complaint

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa's debit card is stolen. She reports it within 2 business days of noticing. Thieves spent $700. What is her most liability under federal rules?
questions.intro: Federal rules (Regulation E) limit debit card losses: $50 if you report within 2 business days of learning of the loss; up to $500 if later; and possibly unlimited if not reported within 60 days after the statement. Many banks offer more protection.
questions.feedback: Reported within 2 business days, her liability is at most $50.
questions.topic: Consumer rights and where to get help

misconceptions.C: Uses the limit for later reporting

sources: CFPB (Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6): Liability for unauthorized debit card use is limited to $50 if reported within 2 business days after learning of the loss or theft, up to $500 if reported later, and can be unlimited for later transfers if not reported within 60 days after the statement is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

CFPB (Lost or stolen credit cards): Under federal law, liability for unauthorized credit card charges is at most $50 (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)). (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/am-i-responsible-for-unauthorized-charges-if-my-credit-cards-are-lost-or-stolen-en-29/)
CFPB (Submit a complaint): Consumers can submit complaints about financial products; the CFPB forwards them to companies for a response. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/)

FTC (Cooling-Off Rule): The Cooling-Off Rule lets buyers cancel covered sales of $25 or more at their home, or $130 or more at temporary locations, until midnight of the third business day (Saturday counts; Sundays and federal holidays do not); some sales are excluded. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/buyers-remorse-ftcs-cooling-rule-may-help)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs: New Jersey residents can file consumer complaints with the Division of Consumer Affairs, which enforces the New Jersey Consumer Fraud Act. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/)

CFPB (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.13): A billing-error notice is timely when the creditor receives it in writing at its billing-inquiries address within 60 days after transmitting the statement that first shows the error. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/13/)

CFPB (Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.34): The 30-day validation period starts when the consumer receives the validation information; a written dispute within it pauses collection until verification is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1006/34/)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa's debit card is stolen and used for $700. She reports it 10 days after she learned it was stolen, which is more than 2 business days later but before 60 days after her statement. What is the most she could owe?
questions.intro: Federal rules (Regulation E) limit debit card losses, counted from when you learn of the loss: up to $50 if you report within 2 business days, and up to $500 if you report later. If you do not report unauthorized transfers within 60 days after the statement showing them, you can be liable for later transfers the bank could have stopped.
questions.feedback: Reporting more than 2 business days after learning of the theft raises the limit to $500.
questions.topic: Consumer rights and where to get help

misconceptions.A: Applies the limit for reporting within 2 business days

sources: CFPB (Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6): Liability for unauthorized debit card use is limited to $50 if reported within 2 business days after learning of the loss or theft, up to $500 if reported later, and can be unlimited for later transfers if not reported within 60 days after the statement is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

CFPB (Lost or stolen credit cards): Under federal law, liability for unauthorized credit card charges is at most $50 (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)). (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/am-i-responsible-for-unauthorized-charges-if-my-credit-cards-are-lost-or-stolen-en-29/)
CFPB (Submit a complaint): Consumers can submit complaints about financial products; the CFPB forwards them to companies for a response. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/)

FTC (Cooling-Off Rule): The Cooling-Off Rule lets buyers cancel covered sales of $25 or more at their home, or $130 or more at temporary locations, until midnight of the third business day (Saturday counts; Sundays and federal holidays do not); some sales are excluded. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/buyers-remorse-ftcs-cooling-rule-may-help)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs: New Jersey residents can file consumer complaints with the Division of Consumer Affairs, which enforces the New Jersey Consumer Fraud Act. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/)

CFPB (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.13): A billing-error notice is timely when the creditor receives it in writing at its billing-inquiries address within 60 days after transmitting the statement that first shows the error. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/13/)

CFPB (Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.34): The 30-day validation period starts when the consumer receives the validation information; a written dispute within it pauses collection until verification is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1006/34/)

questions.feedback: The CFPB handles complaints about financial products.

questions.prompt: A debt collector calls Rosa at 2 a.m. and threatens jail. What is true?

choices.text: This breaks federal debt collection rules
Unpaid debts send people to jail
She must pay immediately to stop the calls

questions.correct_answer: This breaks federal debt collection rules
questions.intro: The Fair Debt Collection Practices Act bars collectors from harassment, threats, and calls before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. It also gives you the right to dispute a debt and get validation.
questions.feedback: Late-night calls and false threats violate the FDCPA.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A salesperson sells Rosa a $400 vacuum at her home. Under the FTC Cooling-Off Rule, how long does she have to cancel?

choices.text: No time; home sales are final

questions.intro: The FTC Cooling-Off Rule lets buyers cancel many sales made at their home for $25 or more, or at temporary locations such as hotel rooms or fairgrounds for $130 or more, within three business days. Saturday counts as a business day; Sundays and federal holidays do not. Some sales, such as real estate, insurance, and emergency repairs, are excluded.
questions.feedback: A $400 sale at her home is covered: three business days to cancel.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa's credit card statement sent April 30 shows a $120 charge for an item never delivered. The issuer receives her written dispute at its billing-inquiries address on June 15. Is it on time under the Fair Credit Billing Act?

choices.text: No; disputes must be made within 6 days of the purchase
No; disputes are allowed only before the item ships
Yes; it arrived within 60 days of the statement
Yes, because there is no deadline for billing errors

questions.correct_answer: Yes; it arrived within 60 days of the statement
questions.intro: The Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute billing errors, including goods not delivered. The issuer must receive your written notice at the address it lists for billing inquiries within 60 days after it sent the statement with the error.
questions.feedback: April 30 to June 15 is 46 days, inside the 60-day window.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa receives a collector's validation notice about a debt. Within how many days after receiving it can she dispute the debt in writing and make the collector verify it before continuing?
questions.intro: A debt collector must give you validation information about the debt. If you dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period after receiving it, the collector must pause collection until it verifies the debt. You can still dispute later, but this pause right applies only within that window.
questions.feedback: Dispute in writing within about 30 days after receiving the validation information.
questions.topic: Consumer rights and where to get help
sources: CFPB (Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6): Liability for unauthorized debit card use is limited to $50 if reported within 2 business days after learning of the loss or theft, up to $500 if reported later, and can be unlimited for later transfers if not reported within 60 days after the statement is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/6/)

CFPB (Lost or stolen credit cards): Under federal law, liability for unauthorized credit card charges is at most $50 (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)). (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/am-i-responsible-for-unauthorized-charges-if-my-credit-cards-are-lost-or-stolen-en-29/)
CFPB (Submit a complaint): Consumers can submit complaints about financial products; the CFPB forwards them to companies for a response. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/)

FTC (Cooling-Off Rule): The Cooling-Off Rule lets buyers cancel covered sales of $25 or more at their home, or $130 or more at temporary locations, until midnight of the third business day (Saturday counts; Sundays and federal holidays do not); some sales are excluded. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/buyers-remorse-ftcs-cooling-rule-may-help)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs: New Jersey residents can file consumer complaints with the Division of Consumer Affairs, which enforces the New Jersey Consumer Fraud Act. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/)

CFPB (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.13): A billing-error notice is timely when the creditor receives it in writing at its billing-inquiries address within 60 days after transmitting the statement that first shows the error. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/13/)

CFPB (Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.34): The 30-day validation period starts when the consumer receives the validation information; a written dispute within it pauses collection until verification is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1006/34/)
